simple.meaning: חָלָק (châlâq) is a Hebrew object word meaning “smooth (especially of tongue).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 27:11. The surrounding context includes family, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָלָק (H2509) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: חָלָק (châlâq) / H2509 is traced through Genesis 27:11, Proverbs 5:3, Proverbs 26:28, Ezekiel 12:24 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H2509. chalaq חָלָק adjective smooth — 1 literal חָלָק אִישׁ Gen 27:11 (J), smooth man (opposed to שָׂעִר אישׁ ); הֶחָלָק הָהָר Josh 11:17 ; 12:7 the bald mountain (both D); southern limit of Josephus' conquest, identification dubious; (1) white cliffs 8 miles south of Dead Sea, and (2) Mt. Mâdara southwest from Pass es-‚afâ are proposed, see Di.; as substantive חַלְּקֵינַֿחַל Isa 57:6 (see I. חֵלֶק , 4 ) smooth (stones) of a brook-bed (ravine, wady), i.e. thou worshippest common round stones (contempt., see Che Di). 2 figurative of mouth uttering smooth words חִכָּהּ מִשֶּׁמֶן וְחָלָק Prov 5:3 ; compare 26:28 . 3 as substantive = flattery חָלָק מִקְסָם Ezek 12:24 divination of flattery .

occurrences.englishText: Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, “Behold, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man.
For the lips of an adulteress drip honey.
A lying tongue hates those it hurts;
For there will be no more any false vision nor flattering divination within the house of Israel.
